title: Cooperative KV allocation with continuous-batch-aware vacuuming
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Long-running inference workloads combined with variable sequence lengths are producing steady fragmentation in the KV cache. This increases tail latency, reduces effective memory headroom, and forces fallbacks to smaller model variants under load. Goal: implement a cooperative allocation protocol between the continuous-batcher and the KV allocator plus a low-overhead vacuuming scheduler that reduces fragmentation without violating latency SLOs. Scope: allocator protocol changes, batch-scheduler hints, vacuuming background worker, simulation harness, telemetry upgrades. Out-of-scope: full allocator rewrite, persistent on-disk compaction (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration with continuous-batcher: batch scheduler can communicate per-request small allocation hints to allocator
Fragmentation metric (externalized) reduced by >= 35% on representative production traces in simulation
99th-percentile token latency impact from vacuuming < 3ms (measured on canary infra)
KV cache hit-rate improves by >= 5% for long-tail sessions under mixed seq-length workload
Feature gated with runtime flag and can be rolled back remotely
Unit/integration tests and simulation notebooks committed and passing CI
technical_notes: Introduce soft leases: allocator grants 'micro-lease' ranges to batches to encourage contiguous writes when possible
Batch scheduler emits lightweight affinity hints (sequence-length bucket, estimated KV footprint) via existing RPC headers
Vacuuming worker runs in low-load windows (tracked by autoscaler headroom signal) and prefers hot-slab-preserving compaction to avoid churn
Use a lightweight per-GPU fragmentation estimator (sampled histograms) instead of full heap scans
Fallback path: if allocator cannot respect hint, it returns an allocation token so batcher can split or checkpoint KV writes
Memory model: preserve existing slab boundaries; avoid forcing cross-slab rewrites during normal operation—vacuuming does gradual migration
Simulations use production trace replay (anonymized) with sequence-length distributions and token timing to validate trade-offs
rollout_plan: Feature behind flag initially in staging: enable allocator-side no-op to collect metrics
Run simulations and perf benches; iterate on vacuum heuristics (2 weeks)
Canary rollout on dedicated cluster with low-traffic customer tier (1 week)
Measure fragmentation and tail latency; enable gradual ramp by percentage
Full rollout after two successful cycles and sign-off from SRE and PM
testing_plan: Unit tests for micro-lease allocation and lease expiry behaviors
Integration test where batcher sends affinity hints and allocator returns contiguous allocations (simulated GPU)
Synthetic workload perf runs covering extremes: many short sequences, many long sequences, mixed bursts
A/B canary comparison capturing fragmentation_ratio, cache_hit_rate, and P99 token latency
Chaos test: vacuuming worker killed/restarted during active workloads to verify safety and idempotence
risks: Vacuuming may introduce transient latency spikes if mis-scheduled; mitigated by headroom gating
Affinity hints add RPC surface area and require backward compatibility—plan for degrade-to-default path
Estimator sampling may underreport fragmentation in corner-case distributions; will tune sample rates
Coordination between batcher and allocator adds complexity to failure modes; add defensive fallbacks
